title: Catchment and stream network of the Elbow River above Glenmore Dam, Calgary, Canada

headline.label: catchment of the Elbow River above Glenmore Dam, Calgary

data: NASADEM_HGT version 001 by NASA JPL (2020): 1 arc-second (about 30 m) elevations from the SRTM flight of 11 to 22 February 2000, reprocessed by NASA, in metres above the EGM96 geoid, tiles n51w116, n51w115, n51w114, n50w116, n50w115, n50w114.
method: Read a 94 × 73 km window and reprojected it to 30 m cells in EPSG:32611 by bilinear resampling.
Conditioned the terrain with priority-flood depression filling and derived D8 flow directions and upstream area (pyflwdir), with flow leaving at the window edge.

Placed the outlet on the Elbow River at -114.1080, 50.9930 and moved it downstream to the first cell draining at least 200 km² (399 m), then delineated the catchment above it and checked that it does not touch the window edge.
Streams: every cell draining 2 km² or more, ordered by Strahler; drainage density recounted at 1 and 10 km² to show the effect of the threshold.
limits: Terrain analysis for a hydrology study, not a hydrology or flood study: no rainfall, runoff, discharge or flood level is computed. NASADEM records the surface of February 2000 with about 30 m cells; SRTM-based heights carry absolute errors of about 5 to 9 m (90% level, Rodríguez et al. 2006), more on steep slopes, and include tree canopy and buildings, so streams are least reliable in forest, in towns and on flat ground.
